name: Nem nướng
summary: Grilled pork paste from Ninh Hòa, served in Nha Trang as a rice-paper roll with herbs, pickles, fried ram, and a yellow-orange sauce. The provincial page prints the method and three shop addresses.
origin: Ninh Hòa, in Khánh Hòa. The provincial page tells the visitor to eat it in Nha Trang.
history: The provincial page, citing the culture and sports department and Báo Khánh Hòa, says nem nướng Nha Trang comes from Ninh Hòa.
texture: The page says the pork is ground, seasoned, put on bamboo skewers, and grilled over charcoal. The outside is slightly charred and the inside stays soft.
taste: The page’s words for a bite of the roll are sweet, fatty, sour, tart, and crisp. Those are that page’s words.
howToEat: Lay down a sheet of bánh tráng phơi sương. Add herbs, pickles, fried ram, and half a skewer, then roll it.
The page lists xà lách, diếp cá, hẹ, and other herbs, plus sour starfruit, tart green banana, and pickles.
Dip the roll in the sauce. The page says the sauce is cooked from lean pork, liver, ground shrimp, sticky rice, and fermented bean, and that it is yellow-orange.
where: The provincial page names three rooms and does not rank them: Nem nướng Đặng Văn Quyên at 16A Lãn Ông, Nem nướng Vũ Thành An at 15 Tô Hiến Thành, and Nem nướng Ngọc Tiên at 59 Lê Thành Phương.
A printed portion price on that page is not repeated here. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Nem nướng Nha Trang — the Ninh Hòa roll
seoDescription: What the provincial page says is in a Nha Trang nem nướng roll, how to wrap it, and three shop addresses. No plate photo, and no price copied.
